title: Shahid Ganj and the Opening of Mir Mannu

blocks.text: The battle's cost is counted bluntly here, with the poem stating that five to six thousand Singhs perished in the defeat around Mit Singh's final stand. Enemy victors severed heads for display and loaded as many as eighteen cartloads of severed heads to carry off as trophies for their patrons.

That grim procession did not reach its destination unchanged, because alarm spread near a Ghaggar-side sarai that Sikh forces were approaching. The carts were abandoned there, and Bhag Singh and Bhanga Singh gathered the heads, gave them cremation rites, and preserved the memory of the dead at the place that came to be known as Shahid Ganj.

After closing Mit Singh's martyrdom, the page deliberately shifts tone and opens Episode About Mir Mannu. The new episode introduces the Lahore minister as a persecutor determined to hunt the Khalsa relentlessly, making this page a hinge between memorialization and a fresh cycle of repression.
